newsitem.title: FRANCE: Poll ratings climb for France's Chirac and Juppe.
newsitem.headline: Poll ratings climb for France's Chirac and Juppe.

text.p: Public support for French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe has risen for a third consecutive month from lows in late 1996, according to two separate opinion polls published on Thursday.

One survey, by the Louis Harris institute for Valeurs Actuelles magazine, said 40 percent of those asked had a good opinion of conservative Chirac's performance as president, with 54 percent opposed. In February, the split was 35-55.
It also showed that 33 percent of 1,003 people quizzed on March 7 and 8 had a favourable view of Juppe's performance with 62 percent negative, up from 29-63 in February.
But the poll also showed that 65 percent reckoned that the economic and social climate in France was worsening, against 60 percent in February.

The survey was taken before Chirac staged a marathon television interview on Monday night in which he sought to reassure young people worried by poor job prospects. Youth unemployment is twice the national rate of 12.7 percent.

Forty-one percent of those asked said they would vote for a pro-government candidate if legislative elections were held next Sunday, up from 38 percent in a similar poll in July 1996. Forty-six percent would vote for an opposition candidate, down from 47 percent.

A separate poll, by the IPSOS group for the weekly news magazine Le Point, showed 39 percent of those polled favourably impressed by Chirac's performance compared to 33 percent a month ago. Those with a poor opinion of Chirac dropped to 53 percent from 63 percent.

The number of people with a good impression of Juppe rose from 27 percent to 33 percent while those with a poor opinion dropped from 70 percent to 63 percent, according to the poll conducted on March 7-8 among 950 people.
